sections.title: 1. What this doc is and how it was built
bullets: First of 6 case-study docs, one per H2 9173 topic: 3a Topic 1.1, 3b 1.2, 3c 2.1, 3d 2.2, 3e 3.1, 3f 3.2. H1 8834 topics are the same as H2 Topic 3.1 and 3.2, so 3e and 3f cover H1 as well.

Page 1 lists every case-study slot in Topic 1.1 (15 slots, 17 cases, because strategy slots have a succeeded and a failed case). Slots come from the syllabus content points that ask for a factor, impact, characteristic, strategy, trade-off or challenge.

v0.1 is a preview of the first 3 slots, all in 1.1.1: trade-offs (Amazon deforestation, Brazil), limits on meeting needs (Cape Town 'Day Zero'), and the difficulty of measuring progress (Nigeria's missing census and GDP rebasing).
Each case is about 1 page: a facts table, 1 chart, what happened, how it fits the syllabus point, an exam angle, and numbered source links.
Built with tools/build_case_studies.py from tools/data/case_studies_3a.json; charts from tools/case_charts.py.

sections.title: 2. Assumptions
bullets: 'Sub-topic' in your request (factor, impact, characteristic, strategy, trend, challenges, actors) is taken to mean a case-study slot within a syllabus sub-topic. Topic 1.1 has no trend or actors points; those come up in Topics 1.2, 3.1 and 3.2.
'First 3 sub-topics' is taken to mean the first 3 slots in syllabus order. A succeeded/failed strategy pair first appears at slot 12.
Two slot types not in your list were added because the syllabus uses them: 'Trade-offs' and 'Evaluation' (Malthus vs Boserup).
The image for each case is a chart drawn from the figures in its sources, not a photo. This cloud session's network policy blocks photo sites (commons.wikimedia.org and others).
Web pages could not be opened directly in this session; only web search worked. The figures come from search results that quote each source, and the cited links are the pages those results named.

sections.title: 5. To consider

Reusing one case in more than one slot where it fits well, to cut down on the number of cases to learn.
